editorial.summary: Episode 099 begins as a post-Ranch re-entry document. David distinguishes the first week of isolation, when return remains imaginable and work feels productive, from the second week, when the absence of ordinary contact changes his thoughts and emotional sensitivity. His most reusable Ranch artifact is a chronological DJ set: he plays songs, recalls when he first heard them, and narrates what each one meant, describing the result as Pop-Up Video-like annotations spoken over music. Returning his phone after six days produces a flood of missed messages and private financial requests, which becomes evidence for why disconnection mattered. The episode's title thesis comes from Critter. He describes a nightlife group as a coyote pack whose members have fluid roles, aim to enjoy themselves rather than visibly pursue sex, and treat sexual access as a side effect. The conversation openly exposes the predatory side of that metaphor: targeting perceived insecurity, assigning someone to isolate the sober friend, body-based roles and treating women as obstacles or quarry. Those ideas stay intact, with a separate consent warning. David contrasts this with his own group, which overplanned, sabotaged itself and spent hours analyzing failure. A long autobiographical account connects the end of his seven-year relationship, his decision to prioritize art, roughly a year of repeated self-harm, gambling, a fixation on a private former model, an expensive failed club night, and a later sexual/financial arrangement after her reported opioid addiction. His key archival statement is that honesty and performance coexist: his name is David Choe, but he sometimes plays a `David Choe` character. That distinction should inform every later apparent confession without erasing it. The episode also contains an explicit account of penetration initiated while a sleeping person was unable to consent; the sequence is preserved, not euphemized. Its final third builds an on-air paid-date/sex proposal around Bill Poon and named actresses, including unsupported sexual rumors about Megan Fox.
